brief: A two-storey white clapboard inn with a gabled front, dark shutters, a centre door with a porch hood and a brick chimney, clipped shrubs along the lawn. One photo. Older than 1970: Lake Erie island and harbour-town main streets (the Put-in-Bay model) are 19th-century commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the 'Stagecoach Inn' (Vermilion OH, 1850, remodelled): a white clapboard two-storey house with hipped dormers, black shutters, a fanlit door with an eagle over it, a big exterior brick chimney, clipped round shrubs, a gravel drive; the lake beyond

why.note: an old inn remodelled as a Colonial Revival house
